dialog.body: Public Works storm line, this is Kevin.
Hi, yeah, good morning. I know it's Sunday and City Hall's closed, so I wasn't sure if anybody'd pick up this number. I'm kind of relieved somebody did.
Yep, the storm line's open through the weekend after something like this. What's going on?

So there's a whole tree down. Like the entire thing, roots and all, laying across the side street next to my building. It came down in that coastal storm yesterday, or, well, Friday night into Saturday, and it's still there. I'm honestly worried somebody's gonna drive right into it.
Okay, a full tree across the road. Is it blocking the whole street, or can a car squeeze by?

Wicked close to blocking it. Maybe a little car could get around the top branches on the one side, but it's real tight. And there's power lines nearby, I can't tell if any are touching it. That's what's got me nervous.
Alright, so I'm writing down, tree across the side street, possible lines close by. Can you give me the address or closest cross street?
I'm at 77 Memorial Boulevard, down by Easton's Beach. The tree's on the little side street right next to us.

Sorry, hang on one second, I'm in the middle of unpacking boxes, I just moved in last week, and I need scissors to get into the next one. [pause] Where did I put them. Okay, never mind, I'll find them in a minute. Sorry.
No worries, new place, everything's in a box. Take your time.

Thanks. So my actual question is, who do I even call for this? Is it the city that handles a tree like that, or is it the property owner, or the electric company? Because I don't know whose tree it is, and I'm new here so I don't know who to ring.

Good question. If it's in the street or on city property, that's us, Public Works, and you've called the right place. If it's off a private lot, the tree itself is usually the owner's to clear, but when it's blocking a public road we'll typically get it moved so traffic can pass. And if any wires are down or touching it, that goes to the utility, and you'd keep away from it.
Okay. So I don't need to figure out the owner first before I report it.
No, you don't. You report it to us, we'll sort out whose it is. Do you know which side of the street it came from? Like a yard, or the sidewalk strip?
Um, it looks like it came out of the yard of the house on the corner. It's kind of leaning off their fence. But I couldn't swear to it.
That's fine, I'll put it down as appears to be from the corner property. And for the wires, are you seeing any sparking, or anything hanging low?
No sparking. There's one line that sags a little bit over the branches, but I can't tell if that's normal. I'm not going out there to look closer.
Good, stay back from it. I'll flag that as a possible line issue so the crew checks before they cut anything. Can I get a callback number in case we need to confirm the spot?
Got it, 401-555-0182, and the name?
Gloria Morales. M-O-R-A-L-E-S.

Thanks, Gloria. So that's Gloria Morales, 77 Memorial Boulevard, tree across the side street, maybe from the corner lot, wire sagging nearby. I'm marking it as a road hazard so it goes near the top of the pile today.
Okay, good. Do you have any idea when somebody'll come? I just keep picturing someone coming around that corner in the dark.

Crews are working through a long list from the storm, but a blocked road gets looked at first. Realistically I'd say sometime today or early tomorrow for at least getting it cleared enough to pass. If it's still sitting there tonight, you could call back this line.
Alright. Is there anything I should put out there, like a cone or something? I don't have anything.
I wouldn't go in the road yourself, especially with that line. If you see a car heading for it, that's different, but otherwise leave it to us. If you feel it's immediately dangerous, call 911.
Okay. That makes me feel a little better. Thank you, Kevin, I appreciate it.
Anytime. Hope you find those scissors.
Me too. Thanks, bye.
